messages:
mira: follow-up to the canary/rollback convo. I want to propose an "edge decision shim" that sits adjacent to the router and makes per-request fallback choices locally. Goal: faster degradation and reduced control-plane chattiness while keeping centralized policy as the source of truth.

sam: quick clarifying Q: isn't that basically another flavor of the probe controller?

mira: not quite. probe controller is authoritative and changes the route at control plane. shim is reactive at the edge: it can choose a fallback variant, inject retries, or mirror while leaving the official route unchanged unless controller rolls a new policy.

jiwon: main risk I see is liveliness mismatch: shims in different zones might make divergent choices and cause inconsistent UX. what's the consistency model?

mira: two parts: 1) policy snapshots pushed by control plane carry version ids and an autonomy flag. 2) shim will only act autonomously if snapshot freshness < 30s OR autonomy flag true. Otherwise shim records observations but defers to control routing.

rafa: what signals do shims use? we shouldn't invent heavy heuristics.

mira: keep it small: short-window error-rate (% errors last 60s), moving p95 latency, and queue length. Combine into weighted score; threshold triggers fallback. No fancy ML.

ellen: telemetry and audits are a must. We need to trace which policy snapshot and which local metrics caused a decision.

mira: agreed. shim emits a compact audit event per decision: "shim_decision|policy_v=42|reason=p95>200ms|sample=..." and tags traces with policy_v and decision. Events are batched to the event-writer.

sam: failure modes? If a buggy shim sends everyone to fallback, that's bad.

mira: two layers of defense: 1) router-side delta-circuit: if shim overrides exceed configured delta vs control routing, router disables shim influence and falls back to control routing. 2) per-tenant override_budget tokens: shim decrements a token when it performs an override; if budget exhausted, no more local overrides.

jiwon: sketch the budget API pls.

mira: minimal sketch: "GET /policy/{tenant}" returns "v, autonomy_allowed, override_budget". shim pulls snapshots and keeps a local budget counter. Tokens are refilled periodically or via push when operator changes budget.

rafa: cost/overhead concerns: lots of snapshot pulls or token refresh chatter?

mira: push model for snapshots, opportunistic refresh for counters. No per-request control-plane calls. Audit event egress is batched by shard.

ellen: testing rollout plan? ops needs a safe path.

mira: rollout: observe-only -> shadow-decisions (record-only) -> limited autonomy for small tenant set -> expand. Also include a global kill-switch and per-tenant force-control flag. deploy-bot: canary started us-east-1 (sha: d9f2e). :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary begun for shim v1.0. Metrics endpoints: /dash/shim-decisions, logs in gs://redwood/shim/canary/1798888888

sam: docs and owner expectations are important. "autonomy" needs a tight definition and clear failure behavior.

mira: Agreed. I'll write owner-facing FAQ + an RFC appendix describing invariants and state machine. Also adding an API: "/policy/preview?tenant=x" so owners can simulate local shim behavior before granting autonomy.

jiwon: add a simple ascii state diagram to the PR please: IDLE -> OBSERVE -> OVERRIDE -> COOL_DOWN -> IDLE. Ops should be able to flip COOL_DOWN or global-disable.

mira: will add that. Thanks. Sync tomorrow 10am to walk the token semantics and router circuit thresholds?

rafa: yes, add me.

ellen: I'll join too.

mira: thanks all, prepping PR with code and a short runbook.
